props.rootCause: All cache entries had the same expiry time, so they all expired together and the menu service was flooded (a cache stampede).
props.summary: After #115 added a 10-minute price cache, every store's cache expired at the same moment at midnight. All requests went to the pricing code at once, the menu service ran out of workers, and the app showed 'Menu unavailable' for 47 minutes.
props.title: Menu would not load after the price cache expired at midnight
menu availability below SLO

steps: Check menu error rate and worker count on the menu dashboard.
Warm the cache: `kubectl exec deploy/menu -- python -m menu.cache warm`.
If errors continue, roll back the latest menu release: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/menu`.
Confirm the app shows prices again for two stores before closing.
props.title: Menu not loading: warm the price cache

props.rootCause: The certificate was only read at startup, so the rotated certificate was not picked up until payments restarted.
props.summary: After #120 started loading the card processor's certificate from config, the processor rotated its certificate on a Monday evening. Payments still had the old one, so 60% of card charges failed for 35 minutes during dinner.
props.title: Card payments failed after the processor certificate changed
payments charge failures

steps: Look at the processor response codes in the payments logs (added in #130).
If the failures started after a payments release, roll back: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/payments`.
If it is a certificate problem, restart payments to reload it: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/payments`.
Tell support in #support so they can answer customers, then refund double charges with the Refunds tool.
props.title: Card payments failing: roll back payments

props.rootCause: The connection pool was sized for a normal evening, not a rush.
props.summary: During a big football final, three times the usual number of people ordered at once. #122 had set the orders database pool to 20 connections, which ran out, and 1 in 4 orders failed for 28 minutes.
props.title: Orders failed during the Saturday football rush: orders-db ran out of connections
orders failing

steps: Raise the pool: set `DB_POOL_SIZE=60` on the orders deployment and restart it.
Scale orders to 6 replicas for the rest of the evening.
props.title: Orders failing under load: raise the DB pool

props.rootCause: The gateway's idle timeout was shorter than the gap between location updates when a driver was waiting at a red light.
props.summary: After #123 moved driver location updates to websockets, the API gateway closed idle connections after 30 seconds. Customers saw the driver stuck on the map, and support got 300 'where is my pizza?' messages.
props.title: Driver map froze after the switch to websockets
driver location stale

steps: Check the age of the latest location per active driver on the delivery dashboard.
If updates stopped after a delivery release, roll back: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/delivery`.
Check the gateway's websocket idle timeout is longer than 60 s.
Ask support to tell customers their pizza is on its way.
props.title: Driver map stuck: check location updates

props.text:
# ADR-001: Send new orders to the kitchen through a queue

Status: accepted · Decided: 2026-03-03

## Context
At first, orders called the kitchen screen directly. When a store's wifi dropped, the call failed and the customer's order failed too, even though the payment had gone through.

## Decision
Orders publishes every new order to the order-queue topic. The kitchen, delivery and notifications each read from the queue in their own time.

## Consequences
An order succeeds even if a kitchen screen is offline; the screen catches up when it reconnects. Adding a new reader (like notifications) needs no change to orders. The kitchen can now be a few seconds behind.
props.title: ADR-001: Send new orders to the kitchen through a queue

props.consequences: One place for login and rate limits. The gateway is now tier 1: if it is down, nobody can order.
props.context: The app and the website were each about to call five backend services, each with its own login check.
props.decision: Both talk only to api-gateway, which checks the login once and routes each request.

props.text:
# ADR-002: One API gateway for the app and the website

Status: accepted · Decided: 2026-02-04

## Context
The app and the website were each about to call five backend services, each with its own login check.

## Decision
Both talk only to api-gateway, which checks the login once and routes each request.

## Consequences
One place for login and rate limits. The gateway is now tier 1: if it is down, nobody can order.
props.title: ADR-002: One API gateway for the app and the website

props.consequences: The menu is fast. A price change can take up to 12 minutes to show.
props.context: Working out prices with promos and per-store stock is slow, and the menu is read on every app open.
props.decision: Cache prices for 10 minutes. After INC-2026-002 each entry gets a random extra 0 to 120 seconds so they never all expire at once.
props.title: Cache menu prices, with random expiry times

props.text:
# ADR-003: Cache menu prices, with random expiry times

Status: accepted · Decided: 2026-04-14

## Context
Working out prices with promos and per-store stock is slow, and the menu is read on every app open.

## Decision
Cache prices for 10 minutes. After INC-2026-002 each entry gets a random extra 0 to 120 seconds so they never all expire at once.

## Consequences
The menu is fast. A price change can take up to 12 minutes to show.
props.title: ADR-003: Cache menu prices, with random expiry times

props.text:
Julia Weber: Quick question from a new joiner: why does orders put new orders on a queue instead of just calling the kitchen screen?
Sam Osei: Because store wifi drops. When orders called the kitchen directly, a wifi blip made the whole order fail after the card was already charged. ADR-001 moved it to order-queue in #108.
Rita Gomez: And it means notifications and delivery read the same queue, so nobody had to change orders to add texts.
props.title: Why do orders go through a queue and not straight to the kitchen?

props.text:
Rita Gomez: The processor turns off the v2 API in November, so Maya is moving us to v3 (#135).
Sam Osei: Watch the error codes. v3 renamed some of them, and last time payments broke (INC-2026-003) it took a while to see why.
props.title: Moving payments to the processor's v3 API

props.text:
Nina Larsen: Drivers say the app eats their battery. Tom's #136 only sends a location when the driver has moved 20 m.
Raj Iyer: Sounds good. Just make sure the map still updates while a driver is stopped at a light, we had that problem before.
props.title: Driver app battery drain
